chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Ella arriving in Savannah after a day on the bus
summary: Ella had to dress on the bus before greeting crowds of girls; one-nighters were especially hard on a woman traveling.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I know when we get in Savannah, the bus came in and went down and come around and circled the main street of the colored neighborhood. And everybody was standing with their little girls waiting to meet Ella Fitzgerald, you know.
Now we had been riding all day long, you know. It was hot. And Ella couldn't come out of the bus because her hair was all down (inaudible).
We had to keep her in the back. Then she got dressed -- she'd come out, you know -- she had a welcome committee, you know.
She almost had to get dress on the bus, you know, after you ride all day long. It was really rough on a girl travelling with a band -- you know, like that much, especially in the summertime.
And you get in town, people are standing out there waiting on you to greet you, you know. And here you been riding all half of the night and half of the morning, you know, the heat (inaudible).

Everybody got out the bus and Ella would go back there and fix herself up and, (inaudible), you know. Really rough on a girl.
You know how rough on the men, but it's really rough travelling -- it was really a rough thing. One nighters are really rough.
